name: Preparation H under eyes

lead: Some people dab Preparation H, a hemorrhoid product, under the eyes as a beauty hack, reasoning that its blood-vessel constrictor will temporarily shrink puffiness and bags.

Some versions contain 0.25% phenylephrine, a vasoconstrictor, and shark liver oil; others use 1% hydrocortisone, pramoxine, witch hazel or caffeine, and formulations differ by country. Proponents point to the phenylephrine as the active mechanism: narrower vessels, less swelling. No study of the product on periorbital skin was found, and it is labelled for hemorrhoids.

paras: Posters describe dabbing a thin layer under the eyes, avoiding the lash line, usually shortly before an event, and wiping it off after a while. It is used as an occasional off-label trick rather than a routine.

The product is made for anorectal use, not eyelids. Dermatology references note that medications causing rebound after vasoconstrictors can darken the area, and steroid versions raise skin-thinning concerns. No safety data for periorbital use were found.

angle.text: Users dab the hemorrhoid product Preparation H under the eyes off-label, believing its vasoconstrictor shrinks under-eye vessels and temporarily reduces bags and puffiness. No studies of this use were found.

lead: Preparation H under eyes is an off-label practice in which the hemorrhoid product Preparation H is applied to the skin beneath the eyes, in the belief that it reduces puffiness and bags.

Preparation H is an American brand now owned by Pfizer, sold as gels, ointments, suppositories and wipes; active ingredients vary by country and include phenylephrine, hydrocortisone, pramoxine, witch hazel and caffeine, and some versions contain shark liver oil or yeast extract.[1] Proponents point to the phenylephrine, a blood-vessel constrictor, as the active mechanism.[1]

No study of the product on periorbital skin was found. The only related published work found concerns wound healing in the rectum.[2] Reference material on dark circles notes that medications causing rebound after vasoconstrictors can darken the area.[3]

paras: The original formulation was developed by inventor George Sperti with a yeast extract as the main ingredient; the manufacturer's predecessor acquired the product in the 1930s and it became a leading hemorrhoid treatment.[1] A yeast extract component was removed from the US formulation in 1995 but remained in the Canadian one.[1]

Believers say phenylephrine constricts the small vessels beneath thin eyelid skin and reduces swelling. Whether the product has that effect on the periorbital area has not been tested. Dermatology references describe rebound vasodilation after vasoconstrictors as a possible cause of darkened skin.[3]
The product is labelled for anorectal use. Formulations containing hydrocortisone are corticosteroids, and eyelid skin is thin; no data were found for this use.
No studies found for use under the eyes. A 1984 study examined the product's effect on wound healing in the human rectum, which does not address appearance.[2]

timeline.event: American Home Products acquires a sunburn oil later developed into Preparation H.[1]
Yeast extract removed from the US formulation.[1]
Pfizer acquires Wyeth, the brand's owner.[1]
